title: NSIC Rc 440 (Tubigan 39) Rice Variety: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: NSIC Rc 440 is an inbred rice for irrigated lowland: about 109 days and 5.5 tonnes per hectare on average. See its pest ratings and grain quality.
excerpt: NSIC Rc 440 is an inbred rice variety for irrigated lowland, known locally as Tubigan 39. The NSIC approved it in 2016. It matures in about 109 days and averages 5.5 tonnes per hectare, with a top yield of 10.8 tonnes in trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for rice variety 440, or Rc 440, this is the one. Compare it with the other varieties in our [rice variety finder](/rice-varieties) before you buy seed. blocks.text: How much does NSIC Rc 440 yield?

On average it gives 5.5 tonnes per hectare. That is about 110 cavans of 50 kilograms of palay. It sits above the average of the 118 irrigated lowland inbreds on the list, which is 5.2 tonnes. But the top yield, 10.8 tonnes, came from a trial with good water, seed and care. So plan your costs on the average, then work toward the top with the habits in our guide to [raising rice yield per hectare](/blog/increase-rice-yield-per-hectare).
How many days does it take to mature?

It takes about 109 days from sowing to harvest, and about 102 days if you seed it directly. Varieties of 100 to 120 days count as short duration and 120 to 140 days as medium, so this one counts as short duration. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains turn golden yellow. Because the day count drives every task, anee.io counts it for you from each lot's own planting day, with the [growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.

blocks.text: So scout early for [bacterial leaf blight](/diseases/bacterial-leaf-blight), [tungro](/diseases/rice-tungro), [sheath blight](/diseases/sheath-blight). When you see the first signs, check the guide before you spray, because the right timing saves more than an extra dose. If you are not sure what you see, our [pest and disease finders](/features/pest-and-disease-finders) help you name it from the damage.

Amylose decides how rice cooks. With intermediate amylose, expect rice that is soft but not sticky. In fact, Filipino taste has moved from high to intermediate and low amylose rice, because people want it softer. Head rice is the share of whole grains after milling. So a higher number means fewer broken grains and a better price at the mill.

It suits irrigated lowland, where you control the water. Level the field well so the water stands evenly, and plant together with the farms around you, so pests cannot move from field to field. Our guide to [rice land preparation](/land-preparation/rice-land-preparation) shows each step. It is recommended for the dry season and the wet season. You can plant it dry direct seeded, transplanted or wet direct seeded. For the right month in your province, see [the best time to plant rice](/blog/best-time-to-plant-rice-philippines).

items.q: What is the local name of NSIC Rc 440?
items.a: It is known as Tubigan 39. Seed sellers and agriculturists use both names, so ask for either one.

items.q: How many days does NSIC Rc 440 take to harvest?
items.a: About 109 days after sowing when transplanted, and about 102 days when direct seeded. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains are golden yellow.

items.q: What is the average yield of NSIC Rc 440?
items.a: It averages 5.5 tonnes per hectare, about 110 cavans of 50 kilograms. The best trial reached 10.8 tonnes. Your own yield depends on water, seed, fertilizer and timing.

items.q: In which season should I plant it?
items.a: It is recommended for the dry season and the wet season. Then pick the month with our planting calendar guide and the forecast for your town.

items.q: What should I watch for when I plant it?
items.a: In trials it was weak against bacterial leaf blight, tungro, sheath blight. So scout from the early weeks and act at the first signs.
